findings.title: Stale locks block automated retries
findings.why_it_matters: An installer killed without running its EXIT trap leaves the lock directory permanently. Every later install, update, or uninstall for that prefix exits before doing work and requires a person to verify the PID and remove filesystem state manually, so an agent cannot safely complete a normal retry workflow after an interrupted run.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an explicit non-interactive stale-lock recovery command or flag that records sufficient owner identity to validate liveness, refuses ambiguous cases, and emits a machine-parseable recovery result; retain the current conservative default.
evidence: The lock is removed only from the EXIT cleanup path (lines 81-99 and 388-395), which does not run after SIGKILL or a host crash.
On every lock acquisition failure, line 381 tells the caller to manually verify and remove the stale directory; no CLI recovery path exists in argument parsing at lines 1179-1230.
Both mutating entry points acquire this lock before their operation (run_install and run_uninstall).

findings.title: Doctor output lacks structured format
findings.why_it_matters: Automation that needs to decide whether an install or repair is safe must parse a presentation-oriented sequence of labels and parenthetical prose. Label changes, spaces in paths, and diagnostic wording make programmatic use brittle even though the command is the installer’s primary inspection surface.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a `doctor --json` mode (or `--format json`) that writes one stable JSON object to stdout and keeps warnings/errors on stderr; preserve the current human-readable default.
evidence: run_doctor emits a sequence of human-formatted lines with `printf` at lines 1128-1169.
The doctor argument parser rejects every argument at lines 1201-1203, so it exposes no machine-readable mode.
The output includes free-form values such as paths and browser status in the same textual representation agents must parse.

residual_risks: The mutating commands are otherwise non-interactive: replacement requires an explicit force flag and diagram deletion requires an exact repeated confirmation path.

A global client-registration writer or an installer using another prefix can still change client configuration outside this prefix lock’s scope; the errors are actionable but no cross-prefix serialization is exposed.
testing_gaps: No CLI-level test exercises an interrupted process that leaves a stale lock and then demonstrates a supported, non-interactive recovery path, because no such path exists.
No contract test establishes a stable machine-facing output format for doctor.
